covers.quote: Use tables if they make content easier to read
Use tables for exact values and information that is too detailed for the text.

rules.quote: Use a table only if there isn’t a simpler way to present your content, such as a list, paragraph of text or diagram.
rules.specification: Assess whether the table makes the particular content easier to use. The guidance about exact values and detailed information identifies suitable uses, not a requirement to tabulate every exact value.
rules.violation_condition: A table presents information that could be presented more simply as a list, paragraph or diagram.
when: Exact values and information too detailed for prose are suitable uses of tables.
A simpler presentation takes precedence.
rules.why: G-2 and G-4: consolidate the table-selection instruction, its heading and its stated use cases.

covers.quote: Report them in the body of the text instead.

rules.quote: Don’t create a table for only one or 2 items.
rules.specification: Count substantive information items, not header cells or the total number of cells. The page does not define how to count an item in a multidimensional table.
rules.violation_condition: A table contains only one or two information items.
rules.why: G-4: the prose alternative is the remedy for the same small-table finding.

rules.quote: Don’t make tables with other tables inside them (known as ‘nested’tables).
rules.violation_condition: A table contains another table.
rules.why: Grain test: nesting is one independently identifiable table-structure defect.

rules.quote: For this reason, design tables so they are self-explanatory.
rules.specification: Assess whether the table, including its title, headings and notes, communicates its meaning independently of the surrounding prose. This does not remove the requirement for a cross-reference.
rules.violation_condition: A table cannot be understood without reading the surrounding discussion.
rules.why: Grain test: independent comprehensibility is distinct from the presence of individual table components.

covers.quote: a cross-reference in the text.
Refer to the table in the text
It is essential to refer to a table in the text.

rules.quote: You must still refer to the table in the body of the text.
rules.violation_condition: A table has no reference to it in the body text.
rules.why: G-4: all four statements require the same body-text cross-reference.

covers.quote: Place the table immediately after the reference to it in the text.
In print, the table should be on the same or facing page.

rules.quote: Place the table close to where you mention it in the text and after the paragraph that refers to it.
rules.violation_condition: A table appears before its referring paragraph or is separated from that paragraph rather than placed immediately after it.
when: In print, the table should be on the same page as its reference or on the facing page.
rules.why: G-2 and G-4: proximity, following the reference and print placement are cases of one placement check.

covers.quote: You must give a table:

rules.quote: a title (also called a caption)
rules.violation_condition: A table has no title or caption.
rules.why: Grain test: a missing caption is a separate finding from other missing table components.

covers.quote: You must give a table:

rules.quote: row and column headings
rules.violation_condition: A table lacks row headings or column headings.
rules.why: G-2: row and column headings are the two cases of the required-heading check.

covers.quote: You must give a table:

rules.quote: information (entries)
rules.violation_condition: A table has no substantive information entries.
rules.why: Grain test: an empty table is a different defect from a missing heading or caption.

covers.quote: Don’t use colour as the only way to convey meaning.

rules.quote: Don’t rely on colour as the only visual means of conveying information in tables.
rules.violation_condition: Information in a table is conveyed by colour without another way to identify the same information.
rules.why: G-4: the later colour instruction repeats the same accessibility check.

covers.quote: Use ‘zero’ or ‘nil’ or 'n/a' where there is no data.

rules.quote: Don’t leave cells empty.
rules.violation_condition: A table has an empty cell rather than an explicit value or an appropriate no-data indication.
when: Use an appropriate explicit indication where there is no data.
Zero is allowed only when the true value is zero.
rules.why: G-4: explicit no-data entries are the prescribed alternative to empty cells.

rules.quote: If it is numeric data, use the numeric zero (0).
rules.specification: Read this instruction with the following restriction: numeric 0 represents a true zero, not missing data.
rules.violation_condition: A true zero in numeric table data is written as a word rather than as 0.
when: The entry is numeric data with a true value of zero.
rules.why: Grain test and G-2: the representation of a true numeric zero is distinct from an empty cell or a false zero.

rules.quote: Only use zero if that is the true value.
rules.specification: A checker needs evidence of the underlying value or the missing-data convention. The appearance of a zero alone does not establish a violation.
rules.violation_condition: A table uses zero to represent missing data or another value that is not actually zero.
rules.why: Grain test: a false zero is a factual defect, not a zero-formatting defect.

rules.quote: Publish long and detailed tables separately or in an appendix.
rules.specification: The page supplies no threshold for long and detailed.
rules.violation_condition: A long, detailed table appears in the main body of a print publication instead of separately or in an appendix.
when: Applies to print publications.
rules.why: G-2: separate publication and an appendix are alternative compliant locations.

covers.quote: A single table on a webpage does not need a table number.

rules.quote: number tables
rules.violation_condition: A document uses tables repeatedly but leaves tables unnumbered.
when: Applies when tables are used repeatedly.
A single table on a webpage does not need a table number.
rules.why: G-2 and G-3: repeated use triggers numbering; the single-web-table permission is not a separate rule.

rules.quote: include the table number when you refer to the table in the text.
rules.violation_condition: A reference to a table omits its table number when tables are used repeatedly.
when: Applies when tables are used repeatedly.
A single unnumbered table on a webpage is exempt.
rules.why: Grain test: numbering the table and including that number in a reference are separate missing-text findings.

rules.quote: Ensure that the table number referenced in the text matches the table number in the title.
rules.violation_condition: A table reference gives a different number from the number in the referenced table’s title.
when: The reference and table have table numbers.
rules.why: Grain test: a mismatched number is distinct from a missing reference or missing number.

examples.note: The example refers to the table without repeating its title.

parts.quote: Table 2 shows that average rainfall has …

examples.note: The example repeats the whole title in the reference.

parts.quote: Table 2 (Average monthly rainfall, June 2017 to December 2019) shows that average rainfall has …

rules.quote: Don’t repeat the whole title of the table in the text.
rules.violation_condition: Body text repeats the table’s complete title when referring to it.
rules.why: E-2: the Write/Don’t write pair tests title repetition, not the broader section heading.

rules.quote: Don’t refer to ‘the table below’ or ‘the table above’.
rules.violation_condition: A table reference identifies the table as ‘the table below’ or ‘the table above’.
rules.why: G-2: above and below are two forms of the same positional-reference defect.

covers.quote: consistent with how it’s presented in the text.

rules.quote: Ensure that the information in the text is consistent with the information in the table.
rules.violation_condition: Body text and a table give conflicting information about the same thing.
rules.why: G-4: both instructions describe the same text–table consistency check.

covers.quote: Your text comments on or interprets the table.

rules.quote: Where possible, avoid repeating the text or data in the table word for word.
rules.specification: The page does not define when verbatim repetition is necessary or unavoidable.
rules.violation_condition: The discussion unnecessarily reproduces table text or data verbatim instead of commenting on or interpreting it.
when: Applies where avoiding repetition is possible.
rules.why: G-2 and G-4: interpretation is the alternative to unnecessary verbatim repetition.

rules.quote: Avoid referring to a page number in the text.
rules.violation_condition: A print document refers to a table by page number.
when: Applies to table references in print publications.
rules.why: G-2: the print and table-reference context limits the instruction’s scope.

covers.quote: Be informative, but don’t include too much information.
Use only as much text or data as you need to make sure the table is easy to understand.
relevant to the title or caption

rules.quote: Limit tables to only the information the user needs
rules.specification: Necessity depends on the table’s purpose and users; the page gives no quantity threshold.
rules.violation_condition: A table contains unnecessary information or information irrelevant to its stated subject.
rules.why: G-4: the heading, elaboration and relevance condition identify the same unnecessary-content finding.

covers.quote: Make sure information is:

rules.quote: precise
rules.specification: The page does not specify the required level of precision.
rules.violation_condition: Table information is imprecise or insufficiently specific.
rules.why: Grain test: imprecision is distinct from unnecessary content or unsupported information.

covers.quote: Make sure information is:

rules.quote: from a credible source and backed by evidence
rules.specification: Determining source credibility or factual support may require evidence beyond the document.
rules.violation_condition: Table information lacks credible sourcing or evidential support.
rules.why: Grain test: evidential support is independent of precision and text–table consistency.

rules.quote: Ensure that information in the table is correctly grouped and sits under the correct headings.
rules.violation_condition: A table entry is grouped incorrectly or appears under a heading that does not describe it.
rules.why: G-2: grouping and placement under headings are aspects of the same categorisation check.

covers.quote: The text or data in a table should use the same grammatical form (for example, noun, noun phrase or sentence).

rules.quote: Use the same grammatical form for each entry in a column.
rules.specification: Apply the explicit per-column instruction rather than requiring every column in the table to use the same grammatical form.
rules.violation_condition: Entries within a table column use inconsistent grammatical forms.
rules.why: G-4: consolidate the two parallelism instructions using the more specific per-column wording.

covers.quote: For example, order a list of names alphabetically by family name.

rules.quote: Organise data in a sequential order.
rules.specification: The appropriate sequence depends on the data. Alphabetical ordering by family name is an example, not the only permitted sequence.
rules.violation_condition: Table data lacks an appropriate sequential ordering.
rules.why: G-2: alphabetical name ordering illustrates one application of sequential ordering.

covers.quote: They can be made accessible in HTML and PDF.

rules.quote: Avoid using them in word processing applications.
rules.violation_condition: A table in a word-processing document contains merged cells.
when: Applies to merged cells in word-processing applications.
This restriction is not stated for HTML or PDF tables, where merged cells can be made accessible.
rules.why: G-2 and G-3: the output format limits the merged-cell restriction.

rules.quote: Don’t make tables too long or too wide.
rules.specification: No maximum row count, column count or physical dimension is specified.
rules.violation_condition: A table’s length or width makes it impractical to use.
rules.why: G-2: excessive length and width are cases of the same table-size check.

rules.quote: If you repeat or duplicate information, combine or delete tables.
rules.specification: The page does not distinguish necessary repetition from duplication that warrants combining or deleting tables.
rules.violation_condition: Separate tables unnecessarily repeat or duplicate information.
when: Compare information across tables in the same content.
rules.why: G-2: combining and deleting are alternative remedies for the same duplication finding.

rules.quote: Use simple language in row and column headings for tables.
rules.specification: The page does not define a vocabulary or complexity threshold for simple language.
rules.violation_condition: Table row or column headings use unnecessarily difficult language.
rules.why: G-2: the same language-simplicity check applies to both kinds of heading.

covers.quote: the first row contains the column headings
the first column (also known as the ‘stub’) contains the row headings.

rules.quote: Structure tables so:
rules.violation_condition: Column headings are not in the first row or row headings are not in the first column.
rules.why: G-2: row and column locations are cases of one heading-position check.

rules.quote: The column and row headings must relate to each other so users can make sense of the information.
rules.specification: The required relationship is semantic; the page gives no more specific test.
rules.violation_condition: The row and column headings do not form an intelligible relationship for interpreting the table’s information.
rules.why: Grain test: the relationship between heading dimensions is distinct from heading wording or placement.

rules.quote: Mark up tables to show header cells and data cells.
rules.violation_condition: A table’s markup does not identify header cells and data cells.
when: Applies to formats that support table markup, including web content and PDF.
rules.why: Grain test: semantic cell markup is a separate accessibility property from visible headings.

covers.quote: Complex tables have header cells that span more than one column or row.

rules.quote: If you use a complex table, you must define the column and row groups and mark up the table accordingly.
rules.violation_condition: A complex table lacks definitions and corresponding markup for its column or row groups.
when: A complex table has header cells spanning more than one column or row.
rules.why: G-2: spanning headers trigger the additional group-markup check.

covers.quote: column headings appear at the top of each page
you repeat row headings on each page.

rules.quote: If a table runs over pages when printed, ensure:
rules.violation_condition: A printed continuation page omits the table’s column headings at the top or omits repeated row headings.
when: The printed table spans more than one page.
rules.why: G-2: both heading types are cases of the continuation-page heading requirement.

covers.quote: You may also need to add notes below the table to help users understand the information and where it comes from.
Use notes to tell users:
how to interpret information in the table
what the source of the information in the table is.
Don’t include this information in the table title or caption or in ordinary footnotes or endnotes.

rules.quote: Add notes to provide sources or help interpret the data
rules.specification: Require table-specific notes when source information or interpretative explanation is needed, not notes on every table regardless of need.
rules.violation_condition: Source information or explanation needed to interpret a table is not supplied in notes below the table, including when it is put in the caption or ordinary footnotes or endnotes instead.
when: Notes can apply to the whole table or a particular entry.
Use notes when users need help interpreting the information or identifying its source.
rules.why: G-2 and G-4: sources, interpretation and excluded alternative locations belong to one table-note placement check.

covers.quote: a symbol such as an asterisk (*) or hash (#) for only one note
superscript numbers or letters for more than one note.

rules.quote: To connect the note under the table to the information it refers to in the table use:
rules.violation_condition: A table note lacks the required connection to its referent, or its locator form is inappropriate for the number of notes.
when: For one note, use a symbol such as an asterisk or hash.
For more than one note, use superscript numbers or letters.
rules.why: G-2: note count changes the locator form within one connection check.

covers.quote: Either use all symbols, all superscript numbers or all superscript letters.

rules.quote: Use only one type of note in a table.
rules.violation_condition: A table mixes symbol, superscript-number or superscript-letter note locators.
when: The table has note locators.
rules.why: G-4: the second sentence specifies the same locator-consistency requirement.

covers.quote: abbreviations
notes to superscript locators
general note to the table
source of data (use the appropriate form for author–date or documentary–note).

rules.quote: When writing table notes, list them in the following order:
rules.violation_condition: Table notes appear out of the prescribed order: abbreviations, locator notes, general note, then data source.
when: Order the note categories that are present; the instruction does not require every category.
rules.why: G-2: the ordered categories jointly define one note-order check.

rules.quote: Align notes to the left.
rules.violation_condition: Table notes are not left-aligned.
when: The table has notes.
rules.why: Grain test: note alignment is separate from note width and identifier formatting.

rules.quote: They should not extend beyond the edges of the table.
rules.violation_condition: Table notes extend horizontally beyond the table’s edges.
when: The table has notes.
rules.why: Grain test: the horizontal extent of notes is an independent layout property.

covers.quote: They should be the same font size as the text of the notes so that they are easily found.

tags.violation_condition: A table presents measurements without identifying their unit in the applicable heading or in the title or caption.

when: The data has a unit of measurement.
A unit already supplied in the title or caption need not be repeated in the heading.
rules.why: G-2 and G-3: the title-or-caption alternative is an exception to putting the unit in the heading.

anchor.quote: Choose a clear typeface
anchor.suffix: in a smaller point size than th

tags.specification: The page does not identify acceptable typefaces or a legibility test.
tags.violation_condition: A printed table uses a typeface that is difficult to read.

when: Applies to printed tables.
rules.why: Grain test: typeface clarity and relative point size are independent properties in the same sentence.

anchor.prefix: Choose a clear typeface
anchor.quote: in a smaller point size than the text.

tags.violation_condition: The point size in a printed table is not smaller than the surrounding text’s point size.

when: Applies to printed tables.
The separate minimum-size recommendation still applies.
rules.why: Grain test: relative table-text size can be checked independently of typeface clarity.

anchor.quote: Don’t use a point size that is too small.
anchor.suffix: Although typefaces and sizes va

covers.prefix: a point size that is too small.
covers.quote: Although typefaces and sizes vary, anything smaller than 8 points is too small.

tags.violation_condition: Printed table text is smaller than 8 points.

when: Applies to printed tables.
rules.why: G-4 and E-4: the body supplies an explicit 8-point boundary; it is not an invented threshold.

anchor.quote: Try to keep tables on one page.
anchor.suffix: If you must use a long table:

covers.prefix: Try to keep tables on one page.
covers.quote: If you must use a long table:

tags.specification: The page does not specify how much redesign is required before a page split is considered necessary.
tags.violation_condition: A printed table is unnecessarily split across pages when it could reasonably fit on one page.

when: Applies to printed tables.
Long tables may continue over pages when necessary.
rules.why: G-2 and G-3: necessary long tables are an exception to the one-page recommendation.

anchor.quote: omit the rule at the bottom of the table – this is a visual cue that the table is not complete

tags.violation_condition: A non-final page of a continued printed table has a closing rule at the bottom.

when: A printed table continues onto another page.
Applies to a page where the table is not complete.
rules.why: G-2: the continuation context limits the omitted-rule requirement.

anchor.quote: at the bottom of the table, insert ‘(continued)’ aligned right to the edge of the table

tags.violation_condition: A non-final page of a continued printed table lacks ‘(continued)’ at the bottom right edge of the table.

when: The printed table continues onto another page.
rules.why: Grain test: the bottom continuation marker is distinct from the next page’s repeated caption.

anchor.quote: on the next page, repeat the caption and insert ‘(continued)’ after the table number
anchor.suffix: – for example, ‘Table 3 (contin

examples.note: The embedded example shows the continuation caption, not the instruction surrounding it.

tags.violation_condition: A continuation page of a printed table lacks the repeated caption with ‘(continued)’ after its table number.

when: The printed table continues from a preceding page.
rules.why: Grain test: the repeated continuation caption is one required caption form.

anchor.quote: Don’t use cell or text formatting to convey meaning.
anchor.suffix: It can make the table difficult

tags.specification: Distinguish formatting used to encode substantive meaning from formatting used only to improve readability. Colour-only encoding is covered by the separate explicit colour rule.
tags.violation_condition: Cell or text formatting acts as a meaning-bearing code in a table.

rules.why: Grain test: non-colour cell or text formatting introduces a distinct semantic-formatting check.

anchor.quote: Use lines where they help people read the table.
anchor.suffix: Short tables need only a line a

covers.prefix: hey help people read the table.
covers.quote: Short tables need only a line above and below the header row and at the bottom of the table.
covers.suffix: Longer tables need lines, or sh

covers.prefix: and at the bottom of the table.
covers.quote: Longer tables need lines, or shading of alternate rows (zebra shading), to help people follow the alignment across the table.

tags.specification: The page supplies no threshold separating short and longer tables.
tags.violation_condition: A table lacks the lines or row shading needed to follow its structure: the specified header and bottom lines for a short table, or lines or alternate-row shading for a longer table.

when: Short tables need a line above and below the header row and at the bottom.
Longer tables need lines or alternate-row shading to help users follow rows.
The separate continuation-page rule omits a closing bottom rule where the table is incomplete.
rules.why: G-2: table length changes the appropriate reading aids within one check.

anchor.quote: Ensure there is not too much white space between columns.
anchor.suffix: This makes the content harder t

tags.specification: The page specifies no maximum column gap.
tags.violation_condition: Excessive white space between table columns makes the content harder to read.

rules.why: Grain test: excessive inter-column space is a separate layout defect.

anchor.prefix: s look the same as one another.
anchor.quote: Use the same font, and font sizes, rule (line) thicknesses and colour schemes for tables throughout the document.

tags.violation_condition: Tables within the same document use inconsistent fonts, font sizes, line thicknesses or colour schemes.

when: Compare tables within the same document.
rules.why: G-2: the listed styling dimensions are cases of one cross-table visual-consistency check.

anchor.quote: Provide a summary for complex tables

covers.quote: For complex tables, provide a summary to give people who use screen readers an overview of the information in the table.

tags.violation_condition: A complex table has no summary giving screen reader users an overview of its information.

when: Applies to complex tables.
The page describes complex tables as having header cells spanning more than one column or row.
A summary may describe the rows and columns, measurements and units, or the relationship between rows and columns.
rules.why: G-2 and G-4: consolidate the summary heading and body instruction; suggested summary contents are optional.

anchor.quote: The summary does not provide the same information as the title or caption.

tags.violation_condition: A table summary merely repeats the information in its title or caption.

when: The table has a summary.
rules.why: Grain test: a duplicative summary is a content defect distinct from a missing summary.
